archetype.name: Retooling (injury-wrecked)
archetype.definition: A recent contender whose 2026 core has been gutted by injuries to its quarterback, right tackle, left guard and lead back, leaving a team that plays like a bottom-five unit while it waits for next year.

report.headline: Hurts is gone, the line is patched, and 2-4 looks fully earned
report.take:
This is a franchise that won 14 games in 2024 and 11 in 2025 with a top-ten net EPA both years. The 2026 version is 30th in net EPA and 28th on offense, and nothing in the record is hiding a better team. The two wins came by two and four points over Washington and Tennessee, and the Eagles failed to cover as favorites in both. The four losses since then include a 27-7 beating in Chicago. Wins over expected sits at -1.06, so the close losses to the Rams and Jaguars cost them a little. The point differential still only supports about three wins, so the bad luck is a rounding error, not a mask.

The engine failure is up front. The run game has the league's worst stuff rate (30.2% of carries stopped at or behind the line), 3.14 yards a carry and a 29th-ranked rush success rate. That leaves the offense 31st in overall success rate and working in long-yardage downs. The line problem predates the latest injuries, but it is about to get worse. Lane Johnson is out with a return estimate in February, and Landon Dickerson is on IR with a knee. The last two games produced 22 and 35 rushing yards. Saquon Barkley's hamstring has cost him time, and Tank Bigsby has nearly matched him in carries.

The bigger number the record doesn't show yet is the quarterback. Jalen Hurts started the first five games. He is now expected to miss the rest of the season after imaging found blood clots in his lungs. Tanner McKee's first start was a 25-14 home loss to Carolina with -8.6 passing EPA. Everything from Weeks 1-5 describes a team that no longer exists.

The defense looks better on the scoreboard (16th in points allowed) than on film (26th in EPA allowed). It allows yardage, ranking 27th in yards allowed per game, and it creates nothing: 27th in pressure rate, dead last in QB hit rate, 31st in missed tackles, and 3 takeaways. It survives by keeping things in front of it, holding at 5th in rush TDs allowed and 9th in deep-pass EPA. Strong special teams also help with field position. That bend-don't-break profile is fragile when the offense can't stay on the field; the team ranks 31st in time of possession. The closest precedent in the history block is 2020: a 4-win team with a -5.3 per-game differential and a 28th-ranked offense, nearly identical to today.

strengths.title: Special teams are winning field position
strengths.body: The Eagles rank 6th in special-teams EPA per game. That is the one phase consistently adding value, and it props up both a stalled offense and an overworked defense. Kicking and coverage units don't depend on the quarterback or the line, so this should hold. For a team scoring this little, though, it narrows losses more than it creates wins.

strengths.title: Defense limits the big play
strengths.body: The defense is poor down to down, but it rarely gets beaten over the top or broken for long runs. It ranks 9th in deep-pass EPA allowed and 7th in explosive run rate, and only four teams allow fewer rushing touchdowns per game. That is why points allowed (16th) runs ahead of EPA allowed (26th). It is a real coverage-shell trait, but it leans on red-zone stops and long drives stalling. With no pass rush and poor tackling behind it, expect some of that gap to close.

concerns.title: Season-ending loss of Hurts
concerns.body: Hurts started five of six games and has been ruled out for the rest of the season. That puts McKee in charge of an offense that was already 25th in pass EPA with its starter. McKee's debut produced -8.6 passing EPA in a 25-14 loss, and the supporting cast is thinned at tight end and running back. This is not a slump that regresses upward; it is a structural downgrade for the rest of 2026.

concerns.title: A run game stuffed at the line
concerns.body: The Eagles are last in stuff rate and 29th in yards per carry. Backs are getting only 2.11 yards before contact, so this is a blocking problem first. The last two games netted 22 and 35 rushing yards. Johnson and Dickerson are now both sidelined and Barkley is out with a hamstring, so the trench issue that started with a healthy line is likely to deepen. Without Hurts' legs as a run threat, defenses can sit on it further.

concerns.title: No pass rush, no takeaways
concerns.body: The defense ranks last in QB hit rate, 27th in pressure rate and 31st in missed tackles. With only 3 takeaways, it has no way to flip a game. That is a real flaw, not a fluke: a defense that can't get home or finish plays is relying on opponents to stall on their own. Edge rushers Jalyx Hunt and AJ Epenesa are out and Nolan Smith Jr. is in the concussion protocol, so the rush could get thinner before it gets better.

trend.note: Two narrow, non-covering wins opened the year, then four straight losses. The run game collapsed in the last two weeks, and the quarterback change in Week 6 removed the one player holding the offense together.

nextGame.headline: McKee gets the league's worst pass defense, Prescott gets a clean pocket
nextGame.body:
Dallas is the mirror image of Philadelphia's problems. It has a top-six offense (6th in EPA, 5th in success rate) with a line allowing the 2nd-lowest sack rate. Its defense ranks 31st in EPA allowed and dead last against the pass, and it is also last on third down. The Book makes the Eagles a 4.5-point home underdog (+185) in a division game between two 2-4 teams. On paper this is the softest defense McKee will see all year, but the Eagles' own pass rush, last in QB hit rate, is unlikely to disturb Prescott. The total of 44.5 points to a game where Dallas moves the ball and Philadelphia has to keep pace through the air.

Availability tilts toward Dallas. The Eagles are without Hurts, Lane Johnson and Barkley, and Dickerson's IR return estimate is this week but not confirmed. On defense they are missing Hunt, Epenesa and corner Michael Carter II, Smith Jr. is questionable with a concussion, and tight ends Stowers and Calcaterra remain on IR. Dallas loses corner Cobie Durant and likely linebacker Dee Winters, which weakens a pass defense that was already the worst in the league. Returner KaVontae Turpin is expected to miss the game, while linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is on track to play.

waysToWin.title: Short, quick passing on third down
waysToWin.body: Dallas is last in third-down conversion rate allowed and 31st in EPA on short passes. A quick game that keeps McKee out of long drop-backs plays directly into that. If the Eagles can stay ahead of the chains, this defense hasn't shown it can get off the field. That is the one way this offense can manufacture long drives and win time of possession.

waysToWin.title: Feed DeVonta Smith and Goedert
waysToWin.body: Smith leads the team in targets. Dallas has let opposing top receivers score well above their norms (30th) and has been 30th in EPA allowed to lead tight ends, which sets up Dallas Goedert. Concentrating the volume on the two most trusted targets simplifies things for a backup quarterback. Durant's absence further weakens the secondary.

waysToWin.title: Win the hidden yardage
waysToWin.body: Philadelphia's special teams rank 6th while Dallas sits mid-pack, and Dallas has a -0.7 turnover differential per game, 25th in the league. Shorter fields from the kicking game, plus Sirianni's willingness to go on fourth down, can steal points the offense won't earn on its own. A takeaway or two would swing a game the Book prices at under a touchdown.

waysToLose.title: Prescott throws from a clean pocket
waysToLose.body: Dallas allows the 2nd-lowest sack rate and passes more than expected (8th), and Philadelphia ranks last in QB hit rate with three edge players out or limited. Pass defense is already 24th in EPA and 28th in EPA allowed to top receivers. Given time, Prescott can pick it apart methodically.

waysToLose.title: The run game stalls again
waysToLose.body: Offenses run against Dallas more than usual, but the Eagles have the league's worst stuff rate and are missing Johnson and Barkley, possibly Dickerson too. If early-down carries keep dying at the line, McKee faces third-and-long all day. The defense then wears down on the field again; the Eagles rank 31st in time of possession.

waysToLose.title: Dallas runs through missed tackles
waysToLose.body: Dallas ranks 6th in run success rate, and Philadelphia is 30th in rush EPA allowed and 31st in missed-tackle rate. If Dallas can stay balanced and churn out manageable downs, the Eagles' bend-don't-break approach has nothing to bend against.

nextGame.watch: Whether McKee can convert third downs against a Dallas defense that is last in the league at stopping them. If he can't against this unit, he won't against anyone.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the Eagles to look like the team from Weeks 3-6, not Weeks 1-2. The offense loses its best player and two Pro Bowl-caliber linemen while its run game is already broken, so scoring should settle in the high teens at best. The defense's points-allowed ranking is more likely to slide toward its EPA ranking than the other way. The special teams edge is the one thing that should hold.

The schedule offers some relief. Washington, Dallas twice, Arizona, Indianapolis and Houston all rank 20th or worse on defense, and the NFC East is led by a 3-2-1 Giants team, so the division isn't out of reach on paper. But Pittsburgh, Seattle and an unbeaten San Francisco are on the slate. Winning the soft games will require a quarterback who has yet to show he can carry this group. The realistic range is a finish in the mid single digits, with a division title only possible if McKee clearly improves and the line gets healthier.
swingFactors: McKee's development as a full-time starter
Dickerson and Barkley returning to stabilize the run game
Whether the pass rush gets anyone home once Hunt and Smith Jr. are back

confidence.note: Six-game sample, and the QB change makes most of it less predictive. The direction is clear but the scale isn't.
